crossRefs.note: Don’t reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
Instruct a wise person, and he will be still wiser. Teach a righteous person, and he will increase in learning.
A wise son listens to his father’s instruction, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.
A fool despises his father’s correction, but he who heeds reproof shows prudence.
Flog a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; rebuke one who has understanding, and he will gain knowledge.
Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
A servant can’t be corrected by words. Though he understands, yet he will not respond.
Let the righteous strike me, it is kindness; let him reprove me, it is like oil on the head; don’t let my head refuse…
As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent.

translations.web: A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.
translations.bsb: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.
translations.kjv: A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.
translations.asv: A rebuke entereth deeper into one that hath understanding Than a hundred stripes into a fool.
